Gate L exists precisely because two CI jobs hung 33 minutes against GitHub's six-hour default (scripts/gate_l_ci_jobs_are_bounded.py:8), and it now enforces CEILING_MINUTES=45 on every job (it passed: 5 jobs, 1 workflow file). Nothing equivalent bounds a RUN. Grepping apps/mcp/dma_mcp and packages/shared for timeout|deadline|max_minutes|budget|lease (excluding pool/http noise) yields only: (a) the claim lease in claims.py, DEFAULT_TTL_MINUTES=90, which the module's own docstring calls 'only mutual exclusion' — 'a lapsed lease is taken over SILENTLY; the staged rows are the state' — so lapse is a handover, not a stop; (b) agent_run.py DEFAULT_TIMEOUT=2400s, which bounds ONE DISPATCH, not the run; (c) fetching.py urlopen timeout=30 per request. R27's soft rule (>=40 search-ops -> checkpoint and STOP) is the only run-level budget and it is unenforceable: ledger.py stats, the single tool it names, raises NameError at scripts/engine/ledger.py:125 on every invocation.
note: Gate L is the pattern; no analogue exists for a run.

text: What marks a DMA **final**? Is there a terminal state, or does finality mean "someone stopped working on it"? Trace `runs.status`.
measurement: There is NO terminal state. Queried the live enum: select unnest(enum_range(null::run_status_t)) returns exactly 7 values — INGESTED, CLAIMED, SYNTHESISING, STAGED, PROMOTED, SUPERSEDED, WITHDRAWN. PROMOTED is not terminal: promote.py:378 sets status='PROMOTED', is_active=TRUE, and a later promote for the same entity moves the older row to SUPERSEDED, while withdraw_run moves it to WITHDRAWN. So 'final' is not a state a run reaches; it is the absence of a newer promotion, expressed as is_active=TRUE. Nothing marks an assessment complete, nothing marks it accepted by anyone, and no status distinguishes 'this DMA is finished' from 'nobody has promoted a newer one yet'.
note: Finality = 'someone stopped working on it', exactly as the prompt suspects.

Reproduced the floor case analytically on 3 categories of differing shape using measured N and R25's own structure (funnel = 5 sweep queries + D rich-doc fetches + (1-c)Nq residue volleys + cN contradicts probes; no-funnel = Nq): break-even coverage c* = (5+D)/(N(q-1)) is 4.4% for P2C2 (N=57, doc-rich/largest), 6.0% for P1C4 (N=42, granular, 10 caps at 4.2 subcaps/cap), 9.6% for P3C2 (N=26, smallest) at q=5, D=5. note: The floor case is refuted on the funnel's own arithmetic: a sweep that surfaces nothing still spent its 5 queries and its fetches, so the sign of the claim is inverted. measurement: The +25-32%/+11%/+3% figures appear in exactly 3 places repo-wide, all prose: SKILL.md:58, CHANGELOG.md:176 ("Token math verified BEFORE implementation"), validate_kg.py:175-176 (a comment). `grep -rln "25-32"` over the whole 99-file archive returns those 3 files and no code, no test, no dataset. Reproduced the floor case analytically on 3 categories of differing shape using measured N and R25's own structure (funnel = 5 sweep queries + D rich-doc fetches + (1-c)Nq residue volleys + cN contradicts probes; no-funnel = Nq): break-even coverage c* = (5+D)/(N(q-1)) is 4.4% for P2C2 (N=57, doc-rich/largest), 6.0% for P1C4 (N=42, granular, 10 caps at 4.2 subcaps/cap), 9.6% for P3C2 (N=26, smallest) at q=5, D=5. At c=0 -- the definition of a dud sweep -- the funnel is a pure net LOSS of 3.5% / 4.8% / 7.7% respectively. Solving the claim: "+3%" requires 8-13% sweep coverage, which is not a dud.

measurement: STALE (R31): run-date is not a frozen constant — `grep -rn RUN_TODAY scripts/` -> 5 hits, all `os.environ.get('RUN_TODAY') or date.today()`; `grep -rnE '20(2[4-9])-[0-9]{2}' scripts/engine scripts/deliver` -> 0 hardcoded dates. But it is an unvalidated env var (RUN_TODAY=2019-06 turns a 2019-01 source from ARCHIVAL/1.0 to CURRENT/5.0), and worse, ers_v2.best_date takes max(event_date, publish_date) with no future guard: two runs with IDENTICAL 2019-01 sources, RUN_TODAY=2026-08-28 — honest -> gate FAIL, dq_gaps ['P1C1.4.1:stale_sources_no_currency_probe(2019-01)'] + STALE_SOURCE follow-up (proves the check fires); add ONE fact tagged event_date 2028 / temporal_role 'planned' / aspirational true -> gate PASS, dq_gaps [], followups {} — and ERS core rises 2.7->3.7, total 1.77->2.43 (+37%). FISHING (R28): three-way test on a 90-page report mined for 1 fact — connector web_fetch + no reason -> gate FAIL thin_sources ['E-110'] (control); connector web_search + read_depth fetched -> PASS (out of the gate's domain, and the skill's own golden fixture tags its only read_depth:'fetched' item connector:'web_search', so 0 of 3 items are in-domain); thin_source_reason='x' (1 char) -> PASS. The reason is never judged, though the codebase demands >=30 chars for followups_waived.justification. RESTATEMENT (R33): has_verbatim_run(n=12) catches 5/7 reworded variants but a reordered or lightly reworded restatement escapes, and `if len(fw) < n: return False` makes any fact under 12 words structurally un-restatable — 3 of the 4 facts in the reference ledger are under 12 words. UNCERTAINTY COLLAPSE: implemented uncertainty is `0.2 + 0.15*(hi-lo)` over ceiling hints, reachable set {0.2,0.35,0.5,0.65,0.8} with 0.5 as the no-evidence default; the documented model (per-category base +/-0.3..0.5 plus URF and gap modifiers, cap +/-0.8, 'if exceeded mark Cannot reliably estimate') is not implemented — `grep -rn 'reliably estimate' scripts/` -> 0. ceiling_band_delta DOES apply (verdict delta -2 moved M2-M3 -> M1, BANDS index arithmetic at build_handoff.py:50-51) but a FAILED, provisional challenge still emits confidence 'HIGH' and an unchanged uncertainty 0.35, and `'PROVISIONAL' if v.get('provisional') else v.get('overall')` means the word FAIL never reaches the handoff for a provisional record. No gate requires a challenge verdict to exist at all: floors_gate never reads ledger kind 'verdict', and a run with zero verdicts yields challenge:null and a clean gate.

text: The guarantee is real but its scope is undeclared. The headless failure is not lock contention — it is that headless dispatch has no way to give two workers the same $RUN, so the 'parallel-safe' claim is doing no work and the durable ledger is per-container.
measurement: ledger.py:30-51 mints ids under `fcntl.flock(lf, LOCK_EX)` on `$RUN/01_evidence/.idlock` with the counter in `.idnext`; ledger.py:16-28 appends via a single `os.write` on an `O_APPEND` fd. Both guarantees are filesystem-local: flock coordinates only processes on one host sharing one inode, and O_APPEND atomicity is a POSIX single-filesystem property. SKILL.md:49 states the claim without that qualifier — 'evidence ids MUST be minted via ledger.new_evidence_id(run) (fcntl-locked, parallel-safe)'. Can dispatch span machines? Nothing in either tree shares $RUN across hosts: 0 upload/sync hits in the archive (see S6-13); /home/user/Accelerate/plugins/dma-insights/scripts/agent_run.py (198 lines) runs `subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=repo_root, ...)` — a local child process, not a session — and contains no create_session, environment_id or run-dir handoff; routines.json declares no research dispatcher. So the parallel-agent story in cowork_protocol.md:30 ('Sub-agent brief template — paste when delegating a batch') is safe only for same-container sub-agents, and cross-machine fan-out is not unsafe so much as impossible: a second container cannot see $RUN at all. The one cross-writer detector that exists, ledger.compact's id_collisions (fires when the same evidence_id carries a different url; verified in the smoke test at corrupt_lines==1, id_collisions==1), can only fire on a SINGLE merged ledger, and nothing merges ledgers.
note: The guarantee is real but its scope is undeclared. The headless failure is not lock contention — it is that headless dispatch has no way to give two workers the same $RUN, so the 'parallel-safe' claim is doing no work and the durable ledger is per-container.

That split is the mechanical reason invariant 4 cannot hol
measurement: Ran it: `python3 plugins/dma-insights/scripts/drive_fetch.py check` = "drive preflight OK: 'General DMAs' reachable as dmai-routine@digital-maturity-assessor.iam.gserviceaccount.com; 180 children, 180 client folders". So in an unattended run the credential that opens a document is dmai-routine@, loaded from DMA_ROUTINE_SA_KEY_B64 in the CCR environment (secrets.md §1b) — headless, no human per run. The defect is the scope and the documentation. secrets.md §1b calls that key "Deliberately weak: exactly roles/run.invoker on the dmai-mcp and dmai-api services and roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor on dmai-mcp-path-token … it cannot deploy, read the database, touch storage, or mint other identities." Drive access is not an IAM role, and drive_fetch.py:68 mints `DRIVE_SCOPE = "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive"` — full read/write Drive, not drive.readonly — from that same key (drive_fetch.py:87-95). Over the 180 folders shared with that identity it can create, overwrite and trash, and drive_fetch.py itself exercises the write half (push-bundle / push-memory / push-ledger). Separately the CONNECTOR holds no document credential at all (fetching.py, 0 auth references) and the WORKER's access rests on a one-time manual share: infra/provision.sh:70.
note: Two identities, and they do not overlap: the SESSION can read the internal document (full Drive scope) but cannot register verified evidence; the CONNECTOR must verify the evidence but holds no credential to open anything but the public web. That split is the mechanical reason invariant 4 cannot hold for an internal source. secrets.md §3 ("What is deliberately NOT here") lists what is absent and does not mention the Drive scope at all — the one credential a headless firing holds is the one the secrets doc understates.
